issue: #390-E — timeout:/sudo: nested shells lose strictness, stdin, and their own script

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim (IETF rough consensus)
refuted_claims: The sudo: wrapper also loses set -euo pipefail and needs it re-injected — REFUTED: it wraps the whole script, which already opens with set -euo pipefail; only the timeout: wrapper injects a bare {command}.
Existing tests asserting sudo bash <<FORJAR_SUDO prove the old shape is required — REFUTED: they pinned the literal invocation, not the guarantee; the heredoc is preserved, only the fd changes.
quorum.divergence: the design lane initially proposed re-injecting set -euo pipefail into BOTH wrappers; reading batch_script showed the sudo path already had it, and that claim was killed before implementation.

systems: GitHub Actions — injects `set -eo pipefail` into every bash step precisely because a nested shell does not inherit it
GNU make — .SHELLFLAGS=-ec makes each recipe strict
systemd — ExecStart is a direct exec with RuntimeMaxSec; no shell nesting at all
Terraform remote-exec — one shell, timeout kills the connection rather than nesting
Ansible async/poll — module runs as a separate process with rc captured
crux.verdict: four of five never create the nesting; the one that does injects strictness explicitly. forjar was BELOW the field default, not making a design trade-off. The fix matches the GitHub Actions approach.

agy_teamwork.verdict: the 1.24.0 pre-release review named this the highest-severity open item, called it security-adjacent, and recommended shipping it separately and fast
unique_findings: recommended a separate PR rather than bundling behind a message-formatting change — followed here
